---
title: "A4 self-check — Water and excretion"
---

State the boundary, units and direction before opening each answer. Use the
[tutorial](index.qmd) if you need to rebuild a mechanism.

## 1. What water tendency does a typical freshwater teleost face?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Its internal fluids are more concentrated than surrounding freshwater, so
water tends to enter across permeable surfaces. Ion loss is a separate challenge.
Compensation includes ion uptake and production of relatively abundant dilute urine.
:::

## 2. Does osmoconformity imply every internal ion equals its seawater concentration?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Total osmotic concentration can be similar while selected ions are
regulated. “Conformer” must be interpreted for the variable being compared.
:::

## 3. Is a filtered glucose molecule already excreted?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. It is in tubular fluid and can be reabsorbed. Excretion is the amount
that finally leaves in urine. Filtration, reabsorption and secretion have
different directions.
:::

## 4. Filtered load 10, reabsorption 7, secretion 2 mmol min⁻¹: what is excreted?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

$10-7+2=5$ mmol min⁻¹. All terms are rates of the same substance. Concentrations
cannot be inserted into this balance without the appropriate flow.
:::

## 5. Can ADH action conserve water without creating water?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

Yes. Increased collecting-duct water permeability allows greater recovery
when an appropriate medullary gradient exists. This reduces water leaving
in urine; it does not add new water to the body's total inputs.
:::

## 6. Is concentrated urine necessarily a larger solute loss per minute?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answer

No. Excretion rate is concentration × urine flow. Halving flow while doubling
concentration leaves solute excretion unchanged. Always distinguish amount,
concentration and amount per time.
:::
